steps.description: Fit ~ condition on the filtered counts with median-of-ratios size factors. Pre-filter minimally: keep genes with >= 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size); the independent filter of results() does the rest. Verify the counts are integer-valued (Salmon gene counts can be fractional; round if needed and state so). Set 'control' as the explicit reference level of the condition factor. Run the Wald test with the contrast condition treated vs control. Shrink the reported log2 fold change with apeglm (type='apeglm'). Keep independent filtering on at alpha = 0.05 and adjust with BH; inspect the p-value histogram before trusting the adjusted values. With 6 replicates per condition, DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and sets those p-values to NA — report the flagged genes separately from the independent-filter NAs.

plan.title: Treated vs control heart DE (DESeq2 + edgeR overlap)
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is a single two-group contrast: 6 treated vs 6 control human heart samples, unpaired, one batch, gene-level counts from Salmon (12000 genes x 12 samples). Two data facts drive the design: (1) the libraries are rRNA-depleted total RNA without UMIs, with sequencing QC reporting >60% duplication in most libraries — without UMIs duplicate reads cannot be molecule-counted and must not be removed, so the counts are used as delivered and the duplication rate is reported as a caveat; (2) sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, so sample-structure QC inspects it on PCA and sample distances before any decision to drop it. The DESeq2 path (Wald test, median-of-ratios size factors, apeglm shrinkage, independent filtering at alpha 0.05, BH) is the primary test for 6 replicates per group; an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts is the second method, and the intersection of the two DE gene sets is reported as the high-confidence set. Because the counts arrive as a gene-level Salmon table with no per-sample quantification files and no average-transcript-length table, the model is fitted without a length offset, and the report states that isoform-usage changes could surface as gene-level differential expression.

DESeq2 Wald test, contrast treated vs control
apeglm shrinkage of log2 fold change
BH at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering; p-value histogram inspected before adjustment
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as the second method for robustness overlap
DE report: unshrunken and apeglm-shrunken log2FC with lfcSE, MA and dispersion plots, DESeq2-edgeR overlap, reproducibility record

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

If a sample has a high duplication rate, do not remove the duplicate reads unless the library carries unique molecular identifiers. In RNA-seq the duplication rate follows the expression level, because a highly expressed gene gives many identical fragments. Thus removal without UMIs deletes true signal, and it does not improve the differential expression result. Report the duplication rate of each sample beside its library size and its detected genes. A duplication rate far above the others in a low-depth library is a sign of low complexity, and then the sample is a candidate outlier with a stated reason.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
